spec.title: Re-site the architectural map requirement to 2-review, a checkpoint runs actually occupy
spec.problem: gate-phase-entry.mjs is the only executable requirer of map.json outside the phase that produces it, and it sites that requirement on the `1-ba` row, gated `tiers: ["architectural"]`. `1-ba` is checkpointed BEFORE BA is dispatched and `risk_tier` is BA's output, so since #43 landed (a row carrying a `tiers` key does not apply when the tier is undetermined) the requirement is retired on the mandated path at every tier. Measured at HEAD 52e59f9 in this worktree: an architectural-intent run that never ran Phase 0.5 (no map.json, no `0.5` token in events[]) and whose record carries no determined risk_tier is refused at NO reachable guarded row. The requirement survives only where the tier is ALREADY resolved at `1-ba` -- which on the mandated path means 0.5 already ran and map.json already exists, so the check can catch nothing. The map-skip this row exists to catch is currently uncatchable on the mandated path.
spec.root_cause: The requirement is sited at a phase whose checkpoint is written before the value the requirement is conditioned on exists. #43 correctly made the row abstain rather than resolve an absent tier to the strictest one; the abstention is right and the SITING is what is wrong. Nothing was re-sited when the abstention landed, so the row now looks live and is dead.
requirements: R1. Site the map.json requirement at the `2-review` row. TWO independently measured properties make it the target, and both were the Phase-2 blockers against the previous draft. (a) OCCUPANCY: `2-review` is a phase records actually stop at -- 3 distinct records (.pipeline/17, /40, /61), 4 distinct committed blob-states -- whereas `1-ba-complete`, the issue body's own candidate and the previous draft's target, has NEVER been a persisted `current_phase` in any commit of any ref. See measured_state; see out_of_scope for why the issue's candidate is rejected rather than silently re-targeted. (b) ROUTING: pipeline.md checkpoints `2-review` on the architectural route ONLY (`git grep -c 'current_phase: "2-review"' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` -> 1 hit, the Phase 2 `Checkpoint first:` mandate, and that section states 'This phase runs ONLY when `spec.risk_tier === "architectural"`'). Standard runs route to `2-constraints`, trivial runs route straight to `3-impl`.

R2. The re-sited requirement carries NO tier restriction of any kind: no `tiers` key, no `byTier` key, no new determination signal. The PHASE NAME is the tier evidence, and it is a strictly better one than the record's own `risk_tier` field: `risk_tier` is optional in status.schema.json and NO script writes it (verified: `git grep -n risk_tier -- plugins/pipeline/scripts` returns readers only), whereas `current_phase` is written by the orchestrator following pipeline.md's routing. This dissolves the tier-determination problem rather than relocating it, and it is why R1's premise no longer needs a mechanism that does not exist.

R3. Preserve `2-review`'s existing `spec.json` + `content: "ba-approved"` check AT THAT ROW. This is not a nicety: measured, `2-review` is the ONLY row on the architectural route that both is occupied and carries the ba-approved content check (`2-constraints` carries it but is standard-only by routing; `1-ba-complete` carries a weaker presence check and is never occupied). SWAPPING map.json in for spec.json there therefore deletes the ba-approved gate from the entire architectural route. Measured: at HEAD an architectural record at `2-review` with map.json present and a spec.json carrying no `ba_approved_at` is refused rc 2; under a swap prototype it is granted rc 0, and 12 existing named assertions redden. This REVERSES q2's earlier `swap` recommendation, which rested on measurements of `1-ba-complete` that no longer apply.

R4. Rule explicitly on the `tiers` key on the `1-ba` row: KEEP it, with a comment stating that the rework re-entry is the only thing it still does and that first-visit enforcement now lives at `2-review`. Subject to R5.

R5. The shipped code must not falsify prose this lane may not edit. `plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` publishes `git grep -n 'tiers: \[' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs` and asserts it returns exactly one hit, the `1-ba` row. At the shipped commit that must still hold. R2's no-tier-restriction rule satisfies this by construction: no second `tiers` key is introduced.

R6. Keep the ANCHOR_43 clause byte-identical inside the guard comment block that holds "An unusable risk_tier resolves to the STRICTEST row, never the loosest." SCOPE CORRECTED from the previous draft: #43-K1/K2 pin only the ANCHOR_43 SUBSTRING (`test-gate-phase-entry.sh:1255`, an `assert_contains`), not the sentence it sits inside. The surrounding justification clause 'That default is right for a `byTier` row, which is only reached at a phase where BA has already returned a tier' is editable by this lane -- and under R2 it also stays TRUE, because no byTier row is added and `3-impl` remains the only one. The R6/R7 tension the Phase 2 review raised does not arise at this siting.

R7. Rewrite the guard header so no surviving sentence asserts the map requirement is RETIRED AT EVERY TIER, and so the block states where the requirement now lives and WHY that row -- naming occupancy and architectural-only routing, with a re-derivation command for the routing half (the occupancy half is a corpus census; cite it as a command, never as a count that will rot). Write this prose only against the evidence in measured_state, not against an assumption.

R8. Re-anchor #43-K3 rather than delete it; its own label instructs the next reader to re-anchor. The replacement must DISCRIMINATE (a positive string the block must contain, naming `2-review` as the siting, plus a paired negative it must NOT contain, naming `1-ba` as where first-visit enforcement lives) and must carry its own expiry sentence, so a later move fails it loudly instead of comparing two absences.

R9. Update the test file in lockstep so its literals stay TRUE STATEMENTS rather than stale literals that happen to pass. CITE BY QUOTED LITERAL PLUS A RE-DERIVING COMMAND, never by line number: this file's own header records THREE citation drifts inside this issue's record, and the previous draft of this requirement added a fourth by citing `test-gate-phase-entry.sh:90` -- verbatim `  "1-ba|architectural|map.json|{}"`, the one row R4 says to leave alone. (a) THE FIXTURE CELL to change is the literal `"2-review|architectural|spec.json|$SPEC_APPROVED"`, inside the array opened by the literal `GUARDED_ROWS=(`; re-derive with `git grep -n '"2-review|' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh` (exactly one hit; line 92 at HEAD 9c0b01a, re-derive rather than trust that number). (b) THE FIXTURE FORMAT MUST WIDEN, and this is the work the previous draft omitted (DBA): GUARDED_ROWS is `<phase>|<tier>|<prerequisite filename>|<artifact body>` -- ONE filename per row -- and the AC2 sweep writes exactly that one file, so 'give the fixture a map.json' is NOT EXPRESSIBLE for the `2-review` cell without either a widened field or a per-row special case. Name which is chosen, in the implementation report, rather than discovering it mid-build. (c) THE THREE COUNT ASSERTIONS MUST NOT MOVE -- RE-VERIFY THEM UNCHANGED, do not update them (DBA: the previous draft told the implementer to change counts that must stay put, which invites breaking a control). Under EXTEND no row is added or removed, so `the table under test has 15 guarded rows (8 entry + 7 exit)` stays 15, `14 rows can refuse; the 15th is the no-prerequisite exception` stays 14, and `each row exercised its OWN filename, not one shared one` stays 14. Measured: none of the three appears in the conjunction prototype's red set. Re-derive all three with `git grep -n 'the table under test has 15 guarded rows\|14 rows can refuse\|each row exercised its OWN filename' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh`. (d) THE SIX EXISTING NAMED ASSERTIONS measured to redden under a conjunction prototype -- (i) '2-review (architectural) with spec.json present is GRANTED', (ii) 'and it exits 0' (that cell's rc partner), (iii) 'CONTROL: the same fixture with a SATISFYING spec.json is granted', (iv) 'CONTROL: with no spec.json at all, that same event GRANTS (path (b) attests dispatch)', (v) 'with no spec.json at all, a 1-ba event grants entry to 2-review (path (b) is weaker)', (vi) 'a 1-ba-rerun event resolves to token 1 and satisfies the 2-review row'. Every one is a GRANT-side cell whose fixture never mapped; RE-SITE them by giving the fixture a map.json (which requires (b) first), do not weaken them. Re-derive the red set against the mechanism actually chosen -- a swap prototype reddens 12, not 6.

R10. Pin the tier-determination pair (deferred item 1 from #43's Phase 4 panel, routed here by the issue's own comment): a named assertion must redden if `normalizeTier` gains a normalising transform -- `.trim()`, `.toLowerCase()` -- that the raw-field determination check at the call site does not also gain. Both read KNOWN_TIERS, so adding a TIER stays in sync automatically; a change to the MATCHING RULE diverges silently and nothing pins it today.

R11. SEQUENCING AND SKEW, recorded as a hard constraint rather than a note (DevOps). (a) #61 and #63 must be dispatched and merged SEQUENTIALLY, never concurrently: both edit `plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs` and add fixture families to `plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh`, and R9's GUARDED_ROWS/AC1/AC2 lockstep is exactly the bash-array literal a concurrent second editor leaves silently stale without a merge conflict. (b) The PR body and changelog must state both version-skew cases plainly: an architectural run already parked at `2-review` without a map.json starts being REFUSED at its next turn boundary once an adopting project upgrades past this change (intended, and the refusal message is actionable), and a run already PAST `2-review` is never re-evaluated against it, so a clean upgrade is not proof the hole is closed for that run. (c) BACK-OUT, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO INFERENCE (DBA's migration lens, ruling FAVOURABLE): the change is cleanly reversible and the PR body must say so. The rule table is CODE, not persisted state, so nothing about a stored checkpoint is rewritten. No committed record's meaning changes: every historical record at `2-review` is excluded from evaluation by `inFlight()` (24h + final_verdict), so `.pipeline/17` and `.pipeline/40` decide not-applicable regardless of the row. The down path is a plain revert of the PREREQUISITES literal plus the decideForDir indirection, with no data to unwind, no schema cache to reload and no persisted row shape. And the forward skew in (b) is actionable rather than merely disclosed: the refusal text offers three reachable routes (re-run the producing phase; record a SKIPPED event with a non-empty note; conclude the run).
acceptance_criteria: AC1. ROUTING PIN, fixture stated, routing term DISCRIMINATING. FIXTURE (SecOps B2 -- this was the one AC leaving it unstated, and its grant half was false without it): spec.json present WITH `ba_approved_at`, events[] carrying a `1` token and NO `0.5` token; the map.json column is the only thing that varies. Measured why this matters: with map.json present but no spec.json and events[] empty, all six spellings are REFUSED (naming spec.json), not granted -- so the unpinned form of this criterion was false of the very build it governs. BEHAVIOUR: the re-sited row carries no `tiers` key and no `byTier` key, and its decision is INVARIANT across all six tier spellings (architectural, standard, trivial, absent, null, unrecognised): with map.json present all six are GRANTED; with map.json absent all six are REFUSED naming `map.json`. Asserted over the six spellings, not a representative. ROUTING HALF, restated to discriminate (SecOps B1): assert `git grep -c 'Checkpoint first.*current_phase: "2-review"' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` == 1 AND the PAIRED NEGATIVE `git grep -c 'Checkpoint first.*current_phase: "1-ba-complete"' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` == 0. The naive `git grep -c 'current_phase: "2-review"'` == 1 is KEPT, but only as the documented non-zero control that shows the refined term is the one doing the work: measured at HEAD 9c0b01a it returns 1 for `2-review` and 1 for ALL SEVEN `-complete` literals including `1-ba-complete`, so it gives the identical answer for the chosen row and the row `out_of_scope` rejects for never being occupied. SCOPE OF THE CLAIM, stated so it is not read as more than it is: the refined term partitions 8/7 -- 1 for every one of the EIGHT phases carrying a `Checkpoint first:` mandate (0.5-map, 1-ba, 2-constraints, 2-review, 2.5-design, 3-impl, 4-review, 5-archive) and 0 for all seven `-complete` literals -- so it discriminates a CHECKPOINTED ENTRY phase from a pass-through `-complete` write, which is exactly the mechanistic property `out_of_scope` names. It does NOT discriminate OCCUPANCY: `2.5-design` and `4-review` carry a mandate and have zero occupancy. (SecOps reported this partition as 6/7 by listing the six OCCUPIED entry phases; re-measured here at HEAD 9c0b01a it is 8/7. The finding is unaffected -- the negative half is 0 for every `-complete` literal either way.) EXPIRY, to R8's own standard: if the negative half ever returns non-zero, pipeline.md has begun checkpointing a `-complete` literal, this term has stopped discriminating, and the partition must be re-derived before either half is trusted again.

AC2. THE DEFECT IS CAUGHT. A record at `2-review` carrying `risk_tier: "architectural"`, a spec.json WITH `ba_approved_at`, NO map.json on disk, and events[] carrying a `1` token but no `0.5` token, is REFUSED with rc 2 and the reason names `map.json`. (Measured at HEAD: rc 0, granted. This exact fixture is the run the issue exists to catch.)

AC3. NON-ZERO CONTROL. The identical record with map.json on disk is GRANTED with rc 0; and, separately, the identical record with map.json still absent but a `0.5-map` entry in events[] is also GRANTED. Both halves asserted, so the control cannot pass by being a fixture that always grants.

AC4. THE ba-approved CHECK SURVIVES AT THE SAME ROW. A record at `2-review` carrying `risk_tier: "architectural"`, map.json PRESENT, and a spec.json present but carrying NO `ba_approved_at`, with events[] carrying both `1` and `0.5`, is still REFUSED with rc 2, and the refusal text names `spec.json`, says the file IS present, and diagnoses `carries no ba_approved_at`. (Measured at HEAD: rc 2. Under a swap-at-2-review prototype: rc 0. This is the criterion that forbids the swap.)

AC5. DELTA PRESERVATION, every non-architectural spelling, fixture pinned on the deciding axis. Fixture, stated because the previous draft's silence here was the Phase 2 high finding: spec.json present WITH `ba_approved_at`, constraints.md non-empty, review.json / design.json / impl-report.json / peer-review.json present, map.json ABSENT, events[] = [1, 2, 2.5, 3, 4], updated_at 1h ago. For each of five records -- `standard`, `trivial`, risk_tier absent, `null`, `"Standard"` -- the set of guarded rows returning rc 2 over the full 15-row sweep is IDENTICAL to the set the same record produces at the pre-change commit, except that `2-review` -- that row and NO OTHER -- may be added. The clause is named rather than described because the descriptive form ('a row pipeline.md routes ONLY at the architectural tier') also admits `2.5-design`, `2-review-complete` and `2.5-design-complete`, so a belt-and-braces SECOND siting would satisfy AC5 while `out_of_scope` explicitly forbids one ('One siting, not a belt-and-braces pair'). Two parts of this spec must not be able to disagree about that. Measured baseline at HEAD for all five: exactly {`0.5-map-complete`}. Asserted independently per spelling. Measured delta under the conjunction prototype, independently by SecOps: exactly {`2-review`} at all five non-architectural spellings, so the narrowed clause is what was actually observed, not a tightening beyond the evidence.

AC6. THE UNDETERMINED-TIER ABSTENTION SET IS UNCHANGED, asserted on the OUTCOME rather than on a keyword. With risk_tier absent and NO artifacts present, the set of guarded rows whose decision is `not-applicable` over the full 15-row sweep is exactly {`1-ba`}. This replaces the previous AC8's table half, which was not assertable (PREREQUISITES is `const` and not exported) and would have driven the implementer to a source regex -- a blocklist over a spelling. Measured at HEAD: {`1-ba`}. Verified to discriminate: a second restriction spelled `onlyTiers` on `2-review` keeps `git grep -c 'tiers: \['` at 1 and still turns this set into {`1-ba`, `2-review`}.

AC7. THE PUBLISHED RE-DERIVATION COMMAND STAYS TRUE. At the shipped commit, `git grep -c 'tiers: \[' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs` is 1 and the hit is on the `1-ba` row. (SecOps ruled this half legitimate and NOT the decaying-floor class: it is an exact equality pinned to an identity, guarding a two-file agreement with prose this lane may not edit.)

AC8. `3-impl` IS NOT DISARMED. For each of the three undetermined spellings (absent, null, unrecognised string), a record at `3-impl` with no design.json and no `2.5` token is still REFUSED with rc 2 and the reason names `design.json`. Measured at HEAD: rc 2 for all three. This criterion exists because the obvious discharge of the previous draft's blocker -- gating every byTier row on `tierDetermined` -- silently flips `3-impl` from rc 2 to rc 0 while satisfying every other criterion in this list.

AC9. GUARD PROSE, NEGATIVE HALF. The comment block containing "An unusable risk_tier resolves to the STRICTEST row, never the loosest." contains the ANCHOR_43 clause byte-identically, and contains NO surviving sentence asserting the map requirement is retired at every tier. The existing #43-K4/K5 block-extractor controls must both still be present and passing, so an extractor returning `<no-block>` cannot make the negative half pass vacuously.

AC10. GUARD PROSE, POSITIVE HALF, DISCRIMINATING. A named assertion asserts that same block names `2-review` as where the requirement now lives (positive) AND does not contain a paired near-miss negative naming `1-ba` as where first-visit enforcement lives (negative). Both halves exercised. Its label carries an expiry sentence telling the next reader what to do when it fails.

AC11. MUTATION. Deleting the re-sited map.json requirement from the PREREQUISITES table makes at least one NAMED assertion in `plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh` fail; the set of failing assertion labels is captured, is non-empty, and contains the named label; and that label is unique under `git grep -c` in the tests directory. Print the changed line before running; restore from `git checkout --`, never from memory; commit the real fix first.

AC12. TIER-DETERMINATION PAIR. A named assertion reddens if the pair diverges: with `risk_tier: " architectural"` (leading space) the guard's decision is the undetermined-tier one, and the assertion fails when `normalizeTier` alone is given a `.trim()`.

AC13. THE CONFORMANCE WALK STAYS TOTAL OVER THE WIDENED ROW (DBA blocker). Every token that can satisfy the re-sited `2-review` row -- at every tier, in EVERY sub-structure the widening introduces -- is reachable from the module's EXPORTED surface, so the drift suite's registry-conformance walk sees all of them. That walk is `plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh`, suite `AC18(iv): the satisfying token sets REFERENCE the registry, they do not restate it` (re-derive with `git grep -n 'AC18(iv)' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh`), and it enumerates tokens ONLY through `satisfyingTokens` over `ENTRY+EXIT`. ASSERTED AS AN OUTCOME, not a mechanism: a token that is NOT a member of the imported `KNOWN_PHASES`, planted in ANY part of the `2-review` row, makes that walk RED. MECHANISM of the blindness, stated so the criterion is not read as speculative: `satisfyingTokens` returns `[...row.tokens]` and nothing else (`plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`; re-derive with `git grep -n 'Array.isArray(row.tokens)' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`), so any token held outside `row.tokens` is invisible to every caller of the exported surface, including that walk. MEASURED (DBA, under the `also` prototype): a stray planted in the sub-row's tokens leaves the drift suite 37 passed / 0 failed -- BLIND -- while the identical stray in the PRIMARY tokens goes 36 passed / 1 failed, red on `every satisfying token is a member of the imported KNOWN_PHASES`. WHAT THIS GUARDS, and it is behavioural rather than cosmetic: `eventsSatisfy()` reads the row's tokens, so a stray token there kills path (b) -- the fresh-checkout route the guard's own comment exists for, and the adopting-project population R11(b) is about -- leaving such a record refused with no reachable route. This criterion must exist BEFORE the mechanism is chosen because it CONSTRAINS the choice; which mechanism (a union return from `satisfyingTokens`, a new exported row enumerator) is Phase 2.5's call. PHASE 2.5 CONSTRAINT: if the union route is taken, `#43-S1/S2/S3` must be RE-MEASURED, never assumed -- re-derive with `git grep -n '#43-S[123]' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh`; they walk `satisfyingTokens` over 15 rows x 6 tier spellings, S1 pins `cells` to `${#GUARDED_ROWS[@]} * 6`, and S2 asserts every undetermined spelling returns the architectural token sets byte for byte.
out_of_scope: REJECTED CANDIDATE, stated so a reader of the closed issue is not left to rediscover it -- `1-ba-complete`, the siting the ISSUE BODY ITSELF proposes and the siting the first draft of this spec adopted, is NOT viable and was not quietly re-targeted. It fails on both axes the issue cared about. (a) It is never a persisted `current_phase`: a full census over every commit in every ref, parsing `current_phase` out of every `.pipeline/*/status.json` blob, returns ZERO occurrences across 8 records and 31 distinct blob-states -- as does every other `<phase>-complete` literal the orchestrator passes THROUGH in one write (`0.5-map-complete`, `2-constraints-complete`, `2-review-complete`, `2.5-design-complete`). The discriminator is mechanistic, not sampling: pipeline.md's durable-checkpoint convention makes the exit event for phase N and the entry checkpoint for N+1 ONE write committed together, and the guard is a Stop hook that can only fire when a turn ENDS at a phase. The two `-complete` literals with high occupancy (`4-review-complete`, `3-impl-complete`) are exactly the two where a run naturally pauses. (b) The tier is not determined there either: `.pipeline/34` runs `1-ba`/no tier -> `1-ba`/no tier -> `2-constraints`/`standard`, so risk_tier first appears at the checkpoint AFTER. A requirement sited on a never-occupied row is unreachable in production no matter how green its tests are, and no acceptance criterion catches it, because every gate test forces `current_phase` to the row under test.

HANDOFF, Lane 2/4 -- `plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` is not edited here. Nothing in this spec falsifies it (R5/AC7 keep the published `tiers: \[` grep at exactly one hit on `1-ba`), but TWO sentences become narrower than the truth once this lands and should be APPENDED to, not corrected: the Phase 1 paragraph beginning '**BA's tier is not in the record at this checkpoint, by construction.**' should also tell a reader the map requirement is enforced at `2-review` rather than nowhere; and the Phase 2 section (the `current_phase: "2-review"` checkpoint mandate) should state that entry to that checkpoint now also requires map.json. Re-derive both with `git grep -n "BA's tier is not in the record at this checkpoint" plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` and `git grep -n 'current_phase: "2-review"' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md`.

HANDOFF -- pipeline.md's Phase 0.5 gating prose states that STANDARD runs also produce map.json (BA writes it alongside spec.json in one dispatch) and that only TRIVIAL may skip the deep map. This spec deliberately does not extend the requirement to the standard tier (see q1). Note that the `2-review` siting makes this a structural choice, not a tuning knob: the row is on the architectural route only, so covering standard would need a SECOND siting on `2-constraints` with its own blast radius on the most common tier.

PRE-EXISTING, MEASURED, NOT INTRODUCED HERE, and deliberately not filed under the net-issues-down rule -- the refusal text interpolates `normalizeTier`'s output, so a record with NO determined tier is refused with the literal '(architectural)'. DBA attributed this to the byTier proposal; it is older and wider than that. Measured at HEAD with no proposed change applied: a record at `2-constraints` with an ABSENT risk_tier and no spec.json is refused with '.pipeline/99 at `2-constraints` (architectural) has no `spec.json`...'. It is the guard claiming more than it knows, on every untiered row, today. Folding a message fix into a halting-control diff already at its size tripwire would widen it; folding it in also reddens the refusal-message assertion family. Recorded here with its evidence so the deferral is written down rather than dropped.

The typed `{ tier, determined }` resolver (deferred item 2 from #43's Phase 4 panel). Under R2 the re-sited row reads no tier at all, so this buys nothing for THIS change; R10's assertion remains the cheaper discharge of the pair-divergence risk. Phase 2.5 may adopt it if it falls out of the chosen design.
Widening the guard to require map.json at any phase other than `2-review`. One siting, not a belt-and-braces pair.

Any change to test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh's ENTRY/EXIT/UNGUARDED/TERMINAL populations or to voice-lint's phase vocabulary. Both were checked and are unaffected: the drift suite reported 37 passed / 0 failed under BOTH prototypes.

sibling_causes_considered.name: Other PREREQUISITES rows conditioned on a value not yet written at their own checkpoint
sibling_causes_considered.reason: `1-ba` is the only row carrying a `tiers` key (measured: 1 grep hit) and `3-impl` is the only `byTier` row. `3-impl` is reached long after BA returns. R2 adds no new tier-conditioned row, so the class does not grow.

sibling_causes_considered.name: Rows sited on a checkpoint that is never OCCUPIED at a turn boundary (the class this rework discovered)
sibling_causes_considered.reason: Five of the fifteen guarded rows have ZERO occupancy across every commit in every ref -- `0.5-map-complete`, `1-ba-complete`, `2-constraints-complete`, `2-review-complete`, `2.5-design-complete` -- and every one is a `-complete` literal pipeline.md passes THROUGH in a single write. Their prerequisites are unreachable in production while their tests are green. This spec does not delete them (that is a separate behavioural change and they are harmless), but it refuses to site a new requirement on one, and it records the census as durable state so the next re-siting does not repeat the mistake. Raised as a knowledge_drift_claim so the Librarian can store it.

open_questions.question: Should the pipeline refuse an ordinary standard-tier run that has no blast-radius map, the same way it will now refuse an architectural one?

So a standard run without one has skipped something it was told to do. Answering YES means a SECOND siting on `2-constraints` (the standard route's own checkpoint), not a widening of the `2-review` row, because `2-review` is architectural-only by routing. Standard is the default tier, so YES adds a hard stop to the most common path and NO leaves that path unpoliced.

options.label: No -- architectural only (as specified)
options.implication: Smallest behavioural change, keeps the common path frictionless. Leaves a standard run that skipped its map uncaught.

options.label: Yes -- a second siting on 2-constraints
options.implication: Closes the same hole on the tier most runs use. Doubles the diff, needs its own fixture family, and lands a halting control on the default path -- larger than this issue's tripwire allows.

open_questions.ba_recommendation: No, architectural only, for this issue. The standard-tier map is written by BA in the SAME dispatch that writes spec.json, so the spec.json check already standing at `2-constraints` covers the same dispatch failing -- the marginal catch is small. Widening a halting control onto the default tier deserves its own measurement of how many real standard runs would have been refused, which nobody has taken. Note `2-constraints` has an occupancy of exactly 1 record in the whole corpus, so that measurement matters more than it would have at a busier row.

deploy_notes: This is a hook/gate change that ships to every adopting project via the plugin, not a service deploy -- the project's usual migrations->backend->frontend order does not apply. The relevant blast radius is version skew across the Stop-hook install, not a service topology.

Version-skew behavior on already in-flight runs: gate-phase-entry.mjs's decision is scoped to the run's CURRENT phase only (decideForDir reads status.current_phase, nothing upstream). An architectural run already checkpointed at the re-sited checkpoint (recommended: `1-ba-complete`) that has spec.json but no map.json -- because nothing enforced it before this ships -- will start being REFUSED at its next turn boundary the moment the adopting project's plugin install upgrades past this change, even though the run started under the old, non-enforcing rule. This is the intended fix (closing the exact hole the issue describes) and the refusal message is actionable (produce map.json, record a SKIPPED event with a note, or conclude the run per hooks/stop.sh's fail-CLOSED decision / fail-OPEN tooling split, confirmed by reading hooks/stop.sh and gate-phase-entry.mjs's own `main()`). Flagging only so the shipped changelog/PR description says this plainly, since it is new friction that appears mid-run rather than only on new runs -- an operator with an architectural run parked exactly at that checkpoint should not be surprised by it.

A run already PAST the re-sited checkpoint when the plugin upgrades (e.g. sitting at 2-constraints or later) is never re-evaluated against it -- the guard only judges the CURRENT phase, never phases already passed (confirmed: no historical events[] replay in decideForDir, only current_phase lookup plus the events[]/file check for THAT phase). That is consistent with the file's own documented limit ("It CANNOT prevent a phase being skipped mid-turn") and is not a new gap this issue introduces, but it means an already-in-flight run that skipped mapping and has already moved past 1-ba-complete escapes the fix entirely for that run's lifetime. Worth one sentence in the PR/changelog so nobody reads a clean upgrade as proof the hole is closed for runs already past that point.

Lane-sequencing requirement, called out in the spec's own ba_notes and worth restating as a hard constraint rather than a note: issue #63 is queued in the same lane and also edits plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs (the in-flight ceiling, `inFlight`/IN_FLIGHT_MS) and adds its own fixture family to plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh. #61 and #63 must be dispatched and merged SEQUENTIALLY, not in parallel lanes -- both touch the same PREREQUISITES-adjacent source file and the same shared test file, and a concurrent dispatch risks a silent fixture-count collision (R9's GUARDED_ROWS/AC1/AC2 lockstep is exactly the kind of literal a second concurrent editor can leave stale without a merge conflict flagging it, since bash arrays don't diff the way JSON does).

No coordinated multi-service deploy is required: this is a single file (plus its test file) shipped as one plugin version bump. No feature flag needed -- the change is a stricter refusal on a halting control that already fails open on tooling errors, so a bad rollout degrades to silence (guard disarmed) rather than to a wedged turn, per the fail-open contract in hooks/stop.sh and gate-phase-entry.mjs's own try/catch around main().

concerns.evidence:
